claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by fluorescence microscopy in CLTon cells shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: YFP-G9a-1-618, which lacks the ankyrin repeats, shows significantly reduced interaction with ORCA at the CLTon locus.
claims.source: Interestingly, when CFP-LacI-ORCA was co-transfected with YFP-G9a mutants (Figure 2—figure supplement 1Ba), not only did the mutant YFP-G9a-1-618, which lacks the ankyrin repeats, show significantly reduced interaction but also YFP-G9a-1-965, which has an intact ankyrin repeat but lacks the SET domain, showed significantly reduced association with the locus (Figure 2—figure supplement 1Ba,Bb).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by fluorescence microscopy in CLTon cells shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: YFP-G9a-1-965, which has an intact ankyrin repeat but lacks the SET domain, shows significantly reduced association with the ORCA-tethered locus.
claims.source: Interestingly, when CFP-LacI-ORCA was co-transfected with YFP-G9a mutants (Figure 2—figure supplement 1Ba), not only did the mutant YFP-G9a-1-618, which lacks the ankyrin repeats, show significantly reduced interaction but also YFP-G9a-1-965, which has an intact ankyrin repeat but lacks the SET domain, showed significantly reduced association with the locus (Figure 2—figure supplement 1Ba,Bb).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by fluorescence microscopy in CLTon cells shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: YFP-LacI-G9a triple fusion protein is enzymatically active as evident by the accumulation of H3K9me2 at the CLTon locus.
claims.source: YFP-LacI-G9a triple fusion protein was found to be enzymatically active as is evident by the accumulation of H3K9me2 at the CLTon locus upon the tethering of G9a full-length construct (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by immunofluorescence showing H3K9me2 accumulation at the locus in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: Tethering of YFP-LacI-G9a-ΔSET or YFP-LacI-G9a-H1166K to the locus fails to recruit CFP-ORCA.
claims.source: Tethering of YFP-LacI-G9a-ΔSET or YFP-LacI-G9a-H1166K (a point mutant, which abolishes the catalytic ability of G9a) to the locus (Figure 2Da) failed to recruit CFP-ORCA (Figure 2Da,Db).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by fluorescence microscopy in CLTon cells shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: T7-ORCA can interact with GFP-G9a-ΔSET in co-IP experiments.
claims.source: However, co-IP experiments demonstrated that T7-ORCA could interact with GFP-G9a-ΔSET (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by co-IP experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claims.claim: The interaction of ORCA and G9a at the heterochromatin requires the methylating ability of G9a.
claims.source: These data suggest that while the ankyrin repeat of G9a is sufficient for the association with ORCA (Figure 2Ba), the interaction of ORCA and G9a at the heterochromatin also requires the methylating ability of G9a.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the CLTon experiments showing that catalytically inactive G9a fails to recruit ORCA to heterochromatin.

claims.claim: The interaction between ORCA and Suv39H1 requires the SET catalytic domain.
claims.source: Similarly, the interaction between ORCA and Suv39H1 requires the SET catalytic domain (Figure 2Bb).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by co-IP experiments with Suv39H1 truncation mutants shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: Upon transcriptional activation, there is a striking reduction in CFP-G9a association with the YFP-LacI-ORCA-tethered decondensed locus.
claims.source: In the absence of DOX, ∼80% of cells showed CFP-G9a recruitment to the locus when YFP-LacI-ORCA was tethered (Figure 2Ea,Eb). Upon transcriptional activation, there was a striking reduction (∼10%) in CFP-G9a association in the YFP-LacI-ORCA-tethered decondensed locus (Figure 2Ea,Eb).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by fluorescence microscopy in CLTon cells with and without doxycycline treatment shown in Figure 2E.

claims.claim: ORCA-tethered decondensed locus fails to recruit HP1α but contains Cdk9.
claims.source: ORCA-tethered decondensed locus, in addition to G9a, also failed to recruit HP1α, but contained Cdk9, a component of the pTEFB kinase complex, which is part of the transcription elongation complex (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E)
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by immunofluorescence in CLTon cells shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claims.claim: Orc2 and Orc3 associate with one another at both the condensed and the open chromatin.
claims.source: Two components of the ORC, Orc2, and Orc3 that require each other for their stability associate with one another at both the condensed and the open chromatin (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by fluorescence microscopy in CLTon cells shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claims.claim: The interactions between ORCA and H3K9 KMTs could be dependent on or regulated by chromatin within cells.
claims.source: These results indicate that while ORCA can interact directly with G9a and Suv39H1 (Figure 1Ea,Eb), the interactions could be dependent on or regulated by chromatin within the cells.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that interactions are reduced upon chromatin decondensation in CLTon cells.

claims.claim: Primarily one molecule each of ORC1, G9a, and Suv39H1 interacts with a single molecule of ORCA.
claims.source: After photobleaching analysis of many co-immunoprecipitated YFP-ORC1, YFP-G9a, and YFP-Suv39H1, we found that primarily one molecule each of ORC1, G9a, and Suv39H1 interacts with a single molecule of ORCA (Figure 3Bd,Cd,Dd).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by photobleaching step analysis in SiMPull experiments shown in Figure 3.

claims.claim: In a small population, ORCA associates with two molecules of G9a.
claims.source: In addition, we also observed that in a small population, ORCA associates with two molecules of G9a (Figure 3Cd,Ce), suggesting that the ORCA-interacting-G9a may also be present as a homodimer.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by photobleaching step analysis in SiMPull experiments shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: 39 ± 5% of YFP-ORC1 molecules colocalize with mCherry-G9a in ORCA complexes.
claims.source: After overlaying the two channels, 39 ± 5% of YFP-ORC1 molecules colocalized with mCherry-G9a, indicating that all three proteins, ORC, ORCA, and G9a are found in a substantial fraction of single complexes (Figure 3Ec).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by colocalization analysis in SiMPull experiments shown in Figure 3E.

claims.claim: ∼55 ± 7% of YFP-Suv39H1 colocalized with mCherry-G9a in ORCA complexes.
claims.source: Interestingly, we could observe ∼55 ± 7% of YFP-Suv39H1 colocalized with mCherry-G9a, (Figure 3Fc).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by colocalization analysis in SiMPull experiments shown in Figure 3F.

claims.claim: Sequential IP confirms the existence of ORC-ORCA-G9a in a single complex.
claims.source: We carried out triple transfections of T7-ORCA, HA-ORC1, and Flag-G9a in U2OS cells, followed by immunoprecipitation of HA-ORC1. Following HA peptide elution, the eluate was used for T7-Ab immunoprecipitation. T7-ORCA was immunoprecipitated, and a robust co-IP of Flag-G9a was detected (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C). This further confirmed the existence of ORC-ORCA-H3K9 KMTs in a single complex.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by sequential IP experiments shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: Sequential IP confirms the existence of G9a-ORCA-Suv39H1 in a single complex.
claims.source: Similarly, we performed triple transfections of T7-ORCA, HA-G9a, and Flag-Suv39H1 in U2OS cells followed by immunoprecipitation of HA-G9a. Following HA peptide elution, the eluate was used for T7-Ab immunoprecipitation. T7-ORCA was immunoprecipitated, and a robust co-IP of Flag-Suv39H1 was detected (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D), further confirming the existence of multiple H3K9 KMTs in a single complex with ORCA.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by sequential IP experiments shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claims.claim: ORCA displays increased interaction with mono-, di-, and tri-methylated H3K9 compared to unmodified or K9-acetylated H3 peptides.
claims.source: We found that ORCA displayed increased interaction with mono-, di-, and tri-methylated H3K9 compared to unmodified or K9-acetylated H3 peptides (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by peptide pull-down experiments shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: ORCA has the highest affinity for H3K9me3 followed by me2 and me1.
claims.source: Analysis of the average number of molecules pulled down by the peptides revealed that ORCA has the highest affinity for H3K9me3 followed by for me2 and me1 (Figure 4Ab,Ac).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by quantitative SiMPull analysis with histone peptides shown in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: YFP-ORCA 1–127 aa shows low-basal binding to all the H3K9 methylated peptides.
claims.source: YFP-ORCA 1–127 aa showed a low-basal binding to all the peptides corroborating the necessity of WD domain of ORCA for specifically recognizing methylated histones.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by SiMPull analysis with the ORCA truncation mutant lacking the WD domain.

claims.claim: Upon depletion of ORCA, the levels of H3K9me2 decrease in both U2OS and WI-38 cells.
claims.source: In both the cell lines, upon depletion of ORCA, the levels of H3K9me2 decreased while H3K9me3 remained unchanged at the resolution of Western blotting (Figure 4Ba,Bb).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by Western blotting of chromatin fractions shown in Figure 4B.

claims.claim: Upon depletion of ORCA, H3K9me3 levels remain unchanged at the resolution of Western blotting.
claims.source: In both the cell lines, upon depletion of ORCA, the levels of H3K9me2 decreased while H3K9me3 remained unchanged at the resolution of Western blotting (Figure 4Ba,Bb).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by Western blotting of chromatin fractions shown in Figure 4B.

claims.claim: Around 18% of the detected H3K9me3 peaks show highly significant (more than fivefold decrease) changes upon ORCA KD.
claims.source: Around 18% of the detected peaks showed highly significant (more than fivefold decrease) changes in H3K9 tri-methylation in cells lacking ORCA (Figure 5B, Supplementary file 1 and total H3K9 in Figure 5—figure supplement 1Aa).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by ChIP-seq analysis shown in Figure 5B and Supplementary file 1.

claims.claim: Several regions do not show significant change in H3K9me3 association upon ORCA KD.
claims.source: Interestingly, several regions did not show significant change in H3K9me3 association upon ORCA KD (Figure 5—figure supplement 1Ab).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by ChIP-seq analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: There is a significant reduction of H3K9me3 at satellite repeats upon ORCA KD.
claims.source: Since ORCA associates with heterochromatin, we specifically analyzed the number of reads of satellite repeats in H3K9me3 ChIP and found that there was a significant reduction of this mark at these regions of the genome upon ORCA KD (Figure 5Ca).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by analysis of ChIP-seq reads at repetitive sequences shown in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: H3K9me3 shows less association with telomeric (TAR1) and centromeric (SST1) repetitive DNA in cells lacking ORCA.
claims.source: Furthermore, H3K9me3 showed less association both with the telomeric (TAR1) and centromeric (SST1) repetitive DNA in cells lacking ORCA (Figure 5Cb,Cc).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by analysis of ChIP-seq reads at specific repetitive sequences shown in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: Regions that showed significant reduction of H3K9me3 in ChIP-seq also show significant reduction of H3K9me2.
claims.source: As an alternate, regions that showed significant reduction of H3K9me3 in the ChIP-seq experiment (as evident by the wiggle plots; Figure 5Da–Dd and Figure 5—figure supplement 1Ba,Bb) were chosen for H3K9me2 ChIP-qPCR (quantitative PCR) validation (Supplementary file 2). These regions also consistently showed a significant reduction of H3K9me2, corroborating the decrease seen in Western blotting (Figure 5—figure supplement 1Ca,Cb).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by ChIP-qPCR validation shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: ORCA is associated with H3K9-enriched genomic loci.
claims.source: To determine whether the H3K9-targets are directly regulated by ORCA, we conducted ChIP using HA antibody in HA-ORCA expressing stable cell line. This allowed us to address if ORCA is associated with H3K9-occupied genomic sites. We observed a strong enrichment of ORCA at the H3K9-enriched loci (Figure 5Ea), while ORCA binding to C-FOS, a region devoid of H3K9, was comparable to that of IgG (Figure 5Eb).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by ChIP-qPCR experiments shown in Figure 5E.

claims.claim: The total cellular levels of G9a and Suv39H1 are not reduced upon ORCA KD.
claims.source: Our data revealed that the total cellular levels of G9a and Suv39H1 were not reduced upon ORCA KD (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by Western blotting shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claims.claim: Suv39H1 shows a decrease at H3K9me2/me3-enriched loci upon ORCA KD.
claims.source: Suv39H1 showed a decrease at these loci (Figure 5Fa,Fb), indicating that the loading of Suv39H1 to these regions is reduced upon ORCA depletion.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by ChIP-qPCR experiments shown in Figure 5F.

claims.claim: G9a association with H3K9me2/me3-enriched regions shows either no alteration or an increase at some regions upon ORCA KD.
claims.source: G9a association with these regions showed either no alteration or an increase at some regions (Figure 5—figure supplement 1Ea,Eb), indicating that the reduction in H3K9me2 that was observed was possibly due to impaired catalytic activity of G9a.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by ChIP-qPCR experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1E.

claims.claim: ORCA KD leads to close to 50% reduction of Suv39H1 that co-immunoprecipitates with G9a.
claims.source: ORCA KD showed close to 50% reduction of Suv39H1 that co-immunoprecipitated with G9a (Figure 6Aa,Ab).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by co-IP experiments in ORCA-depleted cells shown in Figure 6A.

claims.claim: ORCA KD leads to ∼50% reduction in the complexes containing YFP-Suv39H1 and mCherry-G9a.
claims.source: ORCA KD led to ∼50% reduction in the complexes containing YFP-Suv39H1 and mCherry-G9a (note, 24 ± 3% mCherry-G9a pulled down by YFP-Suv39H1 in control vs 15 ± 1% in ORCA knock-down cells; Figure 6Bc).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by SiMPull experiments in ORCA-depleted cells shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: The presence of full-length T7-ORCA shows 25 ± 1% association between Suv39H1 and G9a.
claims.source: The presence of full-length T7-ORCA showed 25 ± 1% association between Suv39H1 and G9A.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by SiMPull experiments with ORCA overexpression shown in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: The mutant T7-ORCA (1–270) shows 14 ± 3% of mCherry-G9a in complex with YFP-Suv39H1.
claims.source: The mutant T7-ORCA (1–270) that does not interact with either G9a or Suv39H1, when expressed along with G9a and Suv39H1 showed 14 ± 3% of mCherry-G9a in complex with YFP-Suv39H1.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by SiMPull experiments with ORCA mutant overexpression shown in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: The T7-ORCA mutant (128–647) stabilizes mCherry-G9a and YFP-Suv39H1 complexes (29 ± 6%).
claims.source: By contrast, the other T7-ORCA mutant (128–647) that interacts with both G9a and Suv39H1 stabilized mCherry-G9a and YFP-Suv39H1 complexes in the cell (29 ± 6%; Figure 6Cb,Cc).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by SiMPull experiments with ORCA mutant overexpression shown in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: At 8 hr and 12 hr time points post-aphidicolin release, ORCA depletion causes dramatic reduction in cells showing late replication patterns.
claims.source: At 8 hr and 12 hr time points post-aphidicolin release, ORCA depletion caused dramatic reduction in cells showing late replication patterns (Figure 7B).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by BrdU immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 7B.

claims.claim: BrdU-PI flow cytometry shows a significant reduction in BrdU incorporation in ORCA-depleted cells without significant changes in the early S-phase.
claims.source: BrdU (Bromodeoxyuridine)-PI flow cytometry results showed a significant reduction in BrdU incorporation in ORCA-depleted cells without significant changes in the early S-phase (Figure 7C).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 7C.

claims.claim: Most of the affected H3K9me3 peaks upon ORCA depletion reside in late-replicating domains.
claims.source: Upon ORCA depletion, most of the affected H3K9me3 peaks resided in late-replicating domains (Figure 7D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by comparison of ChIP-seq data with replication timing data shown in Figure 7D.

claims.claim: Changes in replication timing of CELSR3 and FAM20A loci occur upon loss of ORCA.
claims.source: We observed changes in replication timing of these loci (Figure 7—figure supplement 1Cb,Cc shows two representative loci CELSR3 and FAM20A) upon loss of ORCA.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by BrdU ChIP experiments shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: The replication timing of C-FOS remains unaffected upon loss of ORCA.
claims.source: The replication timing of C-FOS, a region that serves as a control showing no changes in H3K9me2 and me3 upon loss of ORCA, remains unaffected (Figure 7—figure supplement 1Ca), suggesting that the replication timing changes observed in ORCA-depleted cells may not be because of the direct role of ORCA/ORC in establishing the pre-replicative complex.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by BrdU ChIP experiments shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: DD-T7-ORCA-siRNA NTV can efficiently rescue ORC2 levels on chromatin upon depletion of endogenous ORCA.
claims.source: We observed that while ORC2 loading was affected upon ORCA depletion (levels of ORC2 decrease in the chromatin fraction with concomitant increase in the supernatant fraction), the expression of DD-T7-ORCA-siRNA NTV construct rescued this phenotype by restoring the levels of ORC2 on chromatin to an extent comparable to that of the control (Figure 8C).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by chromatin fractionation experiments shown in Figure 8C.

claims.claim: DD-T7-ORCA efficiently interacts with endogenous ORC2.
claims.source: In addition, we also carried out immunoprecipitation of DD-T7-ORCA and found that it efficiently interacts with endogenous ORC2 (Figure 8—figure supplement 1A), further confirming that DD-T7-ORCA is functional.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by co-IP experiments shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: Specific depletion of ORCA only in post-G1 cells results in reduction in the H3K9me2 levels.
claims.source: Specific depletion of ORCA only in post-G1 cells also resulted in reduction in the H3K9me2 levels (Figure 8D).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by Western blotting after proteotuner-mediated ORCA depletion shown in Figure 8D.

claims.claim: Depletion of ORCA in post-G1 cells results in a decrease in cells showing mid- and late- patterns of DNA replication and a concomitant increase in cells showing early patterns.
claims.source: In these cells, we examined the replication patterning by BrdU immunofluorescence. We observed a decrease in cells showing mid- and late- patterns of DNA replication and a concomitant increase in cells showing early patterns (Figure 8Eb), similar to our previous observations (Figure 7B).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by BrdU immunofluorescence after proteotuner-mediated ORCA depletion shown in Figure 8E.

claims.claim: In cells lacking ORCA, a large number of cells showing mid-replication patterns show BrdU staining preferentially at perinucleolar regions.
claims.source: In cells lacking ORCA, a large number of cells showing mid-replication patterns showed BrdU staining preferentially at perinucleolar regions (Figure 8Ea, Figure 8—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by BrdU immunofluorescence shown in Figure 8E.

claims.claim: H3K9me3 and HP1α are mislocalized and form perinucleolar rings in cells lacking ORCA.
claims.source: Furthermore, we observed that H3K9me3 and HP1α were mislocalized and formed perinucleolar rings in cells lacking ORCA (Figure 8Fa,Fb, Figure 8—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by immunofluorescence shown in Figure 8F.

claims.claim: Both control and ORCA-depleted cells progress through S-phase at comparable rates.
claims.source: Moreover, both control and ORCA-depleted cells progressed through S-phase at comparable rates (Figure 8—figure supplement 1D) indicating that the observed defects in HP1α localization and BrdU incorporation upon loss of ORCA are due to defects in heterochromatin and not due to indirect effects of defects in S-phase progression.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1D.

claims.claim: The observed defects in heterochromatin organization in ORCA-depleted post-G1 cells are independent of ORCA's known functions in preRC assembly.
claims.source: Based on the results, we propose that the observed defects in heterochromatin organization in ORCA-depleted post-G1 cells are independent of its known functions in preRC assembly.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the proteotuner experiments showing heterochromatin defects when ORCA is depleted after G1.

claims.claim: ORCA is a scaffold protein that stabilizes the H3K9 KMT complex.
claims.source: We demonstrate that ORCA-ORC associates with the H3K9 KMT-containing complex and in the absence of ORCA, this complex disintegrates. The loss of the enzymatic activity of this complex causes changes in the H3K9me2 and H3K9me3 profile in human cells. Based on this, we propose that ORCA is a scaffold protein that stabilizes the H3K9 KMT complex.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental observations including SiMPull and ChIP experiments.

claims.claim: ORCA associates with pericentric heterochromatin via its association to H3K9me3 and maintains silencing at the major satellite repeats in mouse cells.
claims.source: Recent work suggests that in mouse cells ORCA associates with pericentric heterochromatin via its association to H3K9me3 and maintains silencing at the major satellite repeats (Chan and Zhang, 2012).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation to previous work.

claims.claim: The changes in transcription of satellite repeats upon ORCA-depletion are likely caused by the changes in the heterochromatin structure.
claims.source: Based on our results, we speculate that the changes in transcription of satellite repeats upon ORCA-depletion are likely caused by the changes in the heterochromatin structure.
claims.evidence: This is a speculation based on the observed changes in heterochromatin structure.

claims.claim: Ankyrin repeats of G9a contain methyl-lysine binding modules and can generate as well as read the same epigenetic mark.
claims.source: Ankyrin repeats of G9a also contain methyl-lysine binding modules and can therefore generate as well as read the same epigenetic mark (Collins et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation to previous work.

claims.claim: ORCA recognizes repressive histone marks, binds to KMTs that facilitate the propagation of the histone mark, and the newly established marks become docking sites for ORCA, resulting in the spreading of heterochromatin.
claims.source: We propose that ORCA recognizes repressive histone marks, binds to KMTs that in turn facilitate the propagation of the histone mark. The newly established marks then become docking sites for ORCA and the whole process is repeated and this results in the spreading of heterochromatin (Figure 9A).
claims.evidence: This is a model proposed based on the experimental findings and illustrated in Figure 9.

claims.claim: H3K9 tri-methylation is a prerequisite for the subsequent H4K20 tri-methylation at the pericentric heterochromatin.
claims.source: It is well established that H3K9 tri-methylation is a prerequisite for the subsequent H4K20 tri-methylation at the pericentric heterochromatin and this in turn sets the chromatin for binding of other key heterochromatin proteins including HP1 (Lachner et al., 2001; Fischle et al., 2005; Stewart et al., 2005).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citations to previous work.

claims.claim: ORCA interacts with Suv420H1 and H2, enzymes that catalyze H4K20 di- and tri-methylation.
claims.source: It is interesting to note that ORCA also interacts with Suv420H1 and H2, enzymes that catalyze H4K20 di- and tri-methylation, respectively (data not shown).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the discussion but data is not shown in the manuscript.

claims.claim: Suv420H2 is a structural component of the heterochromatin and is required for chromatin compaction as well as cohesin recruitment.
claims.source: It has been previously reported that Suv420H2 is a structural component of the heterochromatin and is required for chromatin compaction as well as cohesin recruitment (Hahn et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation to previous work.

claims.claim: H4K20 me1/2/3 is crucial for the regulation and timing of replication origin firing and ORCA and Orc1 directly recognize these chromatin sites.
claims.source: Recently, Reinberg and co-workers have proposed that the H4K20 me1/2/3 is also crucial for the regulation and timing of replication origin firing and that ORCA and Orc1 directly recognize these chromatin sites (Beck et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation to previous work.

claims.claim: Prdm3 and Prdm16, H3K9 mono-methyltransferases, are required for mammalian heterochromatin formation.
claims.source: Work from Jenuwein and co-workers have pointed to the idea that Prdm3 and Prdm16, H3K9 mono-methyltransferases, are also required for mammalian heterochromatin formation (Pinheiro et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation to previous work.

claims.claim: Mono-methylation of H3 at K9 catalyzed by SETDB1 is a favored substrate for Suv39h for K9 tri-methylation.
claims.source: Similarly, mono-methylation of H3 at K9 catalyzed by SETDB1 has been shown to be a favored substrate for Suv39h for K9 tri-methylation, which can then establish heterochromatin (Loyola et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation to previous work.

claims.claim: HP1 associates with heterochromatin in a transient manner.
claims.source: The fact that HP1 associates with heterochromatin in a transient manner has suggested that other perhaps constitutively bound factors contribute to the organization of heterochromatin (Cheutin et al., 2003).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation to previous work.

claims.claim: Pericentric heterochromatin can be generated independent of Suv39h-HP1 binding.
claims.source: In addition, recent work has demonstrated that pericentric heterochromatin can be generated independent of Suv39h-HP1 binding (Muramatsu et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation to previous work.

claims.claim: A transcription factor-based mechanism has been suggested as an intrinsic mechanism for the formation of heterochromatin in mouse cells.
claims.source: A transcription factor-based mechanism has also recently been suggested as an intrinsic mechanism for the formation of heterochromatin in mouse cells (Bulut-Karslioglu et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation to previous work.

claims.claim: In human cells, ORCA facilitates the recruitment, accumulation, and propagation of heterochromatin by a self-sustaining loop mechanism.
claims.source: Based on our results, we propose that in human cells, ORCA facilitates the recruitment, accumulation, and also the propagation of the heterochromatin by a self-sustaining loop mechanism, whereby ORCA binds to specific chromatin marks, associates with Suv39H1, that in turn propagates more H3K9me3 marks, generating more docking sites for ORCA (Figure 9).
claims.evidence: This is a model proposed based on the experimental findings and illustrated in Figure 9.

claims.claim: In the absence of ORCA, the binding of ORC to chromatin is compromised.
claims.source: We previously demonstrated that ORCA can facilitate the binding of ORC to chromatin and in the absence of ORCA, the binding of ORC to chromatin is compromised (Shen et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claims.claim: ORCA binds to H3K9-methylated chromatin and facilitates the recruitment of KMTs as well as other components of ORC and MCMs to these sites.
claims.source: Our data unequivocally demonstrate that ORCA binds to H3K9-methylated chromatin and facilitates the recruitment of KMTs as well as other components of ORC and MCMs to these sites.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experimental observations including ChIP and co-IP experiments.

claims.claim: The regulation of epigenetic modifications by ORCA may provide identity to repressed chromatin and this is crucial for proper replication.
claims.source: It is possible that the regulation of these epigenetic modifications by ORCA may provide identity to repressed chromatin and this in turn is crucial for proper replication.
claims.evidence: This is a speculation based on the observed effects of ORCA on both chromatin modifications and replication.

claims.claim: G9a mediates di-methylation of H3K9 at late-replicating chromatin predominantly at the nuclear periphery.
claims.source: It is known that G9a mediates di-methylation of H3K9 at late-replicating chromatin and this occurs predominantly at the nuclear periphery.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the discussion as established knowledge.

claims.claim: H3K9me2 and H3K9me3 are enriched at the late-replicating facultative or constitutive heterochromatin, respectively.
claims.source: H3K9me2 and H3K9me3 are enriched at the late-replicating facultative or constitutive heterochromatin, respectively (Wu et al., 2005).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation to previous work.

claims.claim: Loss of Rif1 causes reduction in mid-replication patterns and global changes in replication timing primarily due to Rif1's role in organizing chromatin loops.
claims.source: This is very similar to previous reports that show that loss of Rif1 causes reduction in mid-replication patterns and global changes in replication timing primarily due to Rif1's role in organizing chromatin loops (Cornacchia et al., 2012; Yamazaki et al., 2012; Kumar and Cheok, 2014).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citations to previous work.

claims.claim: ORCA functions as an organizer of heterochromatin, and in cells lacking ORCA replication timing is altered.
claims.source: ORCA could be functioning in a similar fashion as an organizer of heterochromatin, and therefore, in cells lacking ORCA replication timing is altered.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the replication timing experiments and comparison to Rif1.

claims.claim: ORCA is a chromatin reader that facilitates the assembly of the writer KMT complex and its associated partners to specific chromatin sites.
claims.source: Our results demonstrate that ORCA is a chromatin reader that facilitates the assembly of the writer KMT complex and its associated partners to specific chromatin sites.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings showing ORCA binds methylated histones and stabilizes KMT complexes.

claims.claim: ORCA and its associated partners regulate key cellular events, including DNA replication and heterochromatin organization.
claims.source: These together regulate key cellular events, including DNA replication and heterochromatin organization.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings showing effects on both replication and chromatin structure.

results.result: ORCA physically interacts with H3K9 methyltransferases G9a, GLP, and Suv39H1. Endogenous co-immunoprecipitation experiments demonstrate that approximately 1.31% of total G9a and 1.44% of total Suv39H1 exist in complexes with ORCA, representing a higher fraction than previously reported for KMT interactions (0.2%). ORCA does not interact with the arginine methyltransferase PRMT5, demonstrating specificity.
results.evaluation: Claims C27-C33 provide converging evidence from multiple co-IP approaches (endogenous, tagged proteins, stable cell lines) demonstrating specific interactions between ORCA and H3K9 KMTs. The quantification (C28, C29) is based on n=7 and n=4 replicates respectively, and the negative control with PRMT5 (C33) supports specificity. The comparison to prior work (C30) provides appropriate context.

results.result: The interaction between ORCA and H3K9 KMTs (G9a and Suv39H1) is direct and DNA-independent. This is demonstrated by recruitment assays in CLTon cells, co-IP experiments in the presence of ethidium bromide, and in vitro binding assays with purified proteins.
results.evaluation: Claims C34-C36 use complementary approaches (CLTon recruitment, EtBr treatment, purified protein binding) to establish that ORCA-KMT interactions are direct and DNA-independent. The convergence of multiple experimental strategies strengthens the conclusion. The EtBr and benzonase treatments are appropriate controls for DNA-mediated interactions.

results.result: Domain mapping reveals that the WD repeats of ORCA (aa 128-647 and 270-647) interact with both G9a and Suv39H1, while the LRR domain (aa 1-127) interacts only with G9a. The ankyrin repeat of G9a (aa 619-965) and the SET domain of Suv39H1 (aa 151-412) are necessary for ORCA interaction. These interactions are confirmed by both co-IP and CLTon recruitment assays.
results.evaluation: Claims C38-C45 systematically map interaction domains using truncation mutants in both co-IP and CLTon assays. The convergence of results from two independent methods (biochemical and cell-based) strengthens the conclusions. The domain requirements are clearly defined with specific amino acid boundaries.

results.result: The interaction between ORCA and G9a at heterochromatin requires the catalytic activity of G9a. While the ankyrin repeat of G9a is sufficient for interaction with ORCA in co-IP experiments, tethering catalytically inactive G9a mutants (ΔSET or H1166K) to heterochromatic loci fails to recruit ORCA, despite maintaining direct binding capability.
results.evaluation: Claims C46-C50 reveal an important distinction between direct protein-protein interaction (which occurs with catalytically inactive G9a in co-IP, C48) and chromatin-context-dependent recruitment (which requires catalytic activity, C47, C49). This suggests that H3K9 methylation products are necessary for stable ORCA association at heterochromatin, representing a feed-forward mechanism. The experimental design appropriately separates these two modes of interaction.

results.result: ORCA-KMT interactions are chromatin context-dependent. Upon transcriptional activation and chromatin decondensation in CLTon cells, CFP-G9a recruitment to ORCA-tethered loci decreases dramatically from ~80% to ~10%. The decondensed locus also fails to recruit HP1α but contains the transcription elongation factor Cdk9, while ORC components (Orc2 and Orc3) remain associated regardless of chromatin state.
results.evaluation: Claims C51-C54 demonstrate that while ORCA can interact directly with KMTs (established in earlier claims), these interactions are regulated by chromatin state in cells. The CLTon system provides an elegant approach to test this, and the differential behavior of ORC components (C53) versus KMTs (C51) and HP1α (C52) provides important specificity. This reconciles the direct binding data with the chromatin-dependent recruitment.

results.result: Single-molecule pulldown (SiMPull) experiments demonstrate that ORCA-ORC and multiple H3K9 KMTs exist in single complexes. Photobleaching analysis reveals primarily 1:1 stoichiometry of ORCA with ORC1, G9a, and Suv39H1, though a small population shows ORCA associated with two G9a molecules. Colocalization analysis shows 39±5% of YFP-ORC1 colocalizes with mCherry-G9a, and ~55±7% of YFP-Suv39H1 colocalizes with mCherry-G9a in ORCA complexes. Sequential IP experiments confirm the existence of ORC-ORCA-G9a and G9a-ORCA-Suv39H1 in single complexes.
results.evaluation: Claims C55-C60 use the highly sensitive SiMPull technique to provide quantitative stoichiometry and colocalization data. The photobleaching step analysis (C55, C56) provides rigorous stoichiometry determination. The colocalization percentages (C57, C58) are appropriately interpreted considering that not all fluorescent proteins mature and that endogenous proteins may also be present. Sequential IP (C59, C60) provides orthogonal validation. The authors appropriately note this is one of the first demonstrations of three-protein complex detection by SiMPull.

results.result: ORCA preferentially binds methylated H3K9 peptides with highest affinity for H3K9me3, followed by H3K9me2 and H3K9me1, compared to unmodified or acetylated H3K9. The WD domain is essential for this recognition, as the ORCA 1-127 aa truncation lacking the WD domain shows only low basal binding to all peptides.
results.evaluation: Claims C61-C63 use both conventional peptide pulldown (C61) and quantitative SiMPull with immobilized peptides (C62) to establish ORCA's binding preference for methylated H3K9. The SiMPull approach provides quantitative affinity ranking. The truncation mutant analysis (C63) confirms the WD domain requirement, consistent with known functions of WD domains in histone recognition.

results.result: ORCA depletion causes global changes in H3K9 methylation patterns. Western blotting shows decreased H3K9me2 levels in both U2OS and WI-38 cells, while H3K9me3 appears unchanged at this resolution. However, ChIP-seq reveals that ~18% of H3K9me3 peaks show >5-fold decrease upon ORCA knockdown, with significant reductions at satellite repeats including telomeric (TAR1) and centromeric (SST1) regions. Regions showing H3K9me3 reduction also show decreased H3K9me2 by ChIP-qPCR.
results.evaluation: Claims C64-C70 reveal an apparent discrepancy between Western blotting (C64, C65) and ChIP-seq (C66-C69) that is appropriately resolved: global H3K9me3 levels may appear unchanged by Western blot, but specific genomic regions show dramatic reductions. The ChIP-seq analysis is rigorous with >5-fold cutoff for significance. The validation by ChIP-qPCR for H3K9me2 (C70) at the same regions strengthens the conclusions. The focus on repetitive sequences (C68, C69) is appropriate given ORCA's known heterochromatin localization.

results.result: ORCA directly associates with H3K9-enriched genomic loci and regulates KMT recruitment and activity at these sites. ChIP experiments show strong ORCA enrichment at H3K9-marked loci but not at control regions. Upon ORCA depletion, total cellular levels of G9a and Suv39H1 remain unchanged, but Suv39H1 loading at H3K9me2/me3-enriched loci decreases, while G9a association shows no change or increases, suggesting impaired G9a catalytic activity rather than recruitment defects.
results.evaluation: Claims C71-C74 establish that ORCA functions at specific chromatin sites to regulate KMT activity. The ChIP data (C71) confirms ORCA's presence at affected loci. The observation that total KMT levels are unchanged (C72) but chromatin association differs (C73, C74) is important for mechanism. The differential effects on Suv39H1 (reduced loading) versus G9a (maintained/increased loading but reduced activity) suggest distinct regulatory mechanisms and are consistent with the domain mapping showing different interaction requirements.

results.result: ORCA acts as a scaffold protein that stabilizes the multimeric H3K9 KMT complex. ORCA knockdown reduces Suv39H1-G9a complex formation by ~50% in both co-IP and SiMPull experiments. Overexpression of full-length ORCA or the 128-647 mutant (which interacts with both KMTs) increases complex formation (25±1% and 29±6% respectively), while the 1-270 mutant (which interacts with neither KMT) shows reduced complex formation (14±3%).
results.evaluation: Claims C75-C79 provide strong evidence for ORCA's scaffolding function through loss-of-function (C75, C76) and gain-of-function (C77-C79) experiments. The quantitative SiMPull data provides precise measurements of complex formation. The structure-function analysis with ORCA mutants (C78, C79) elegantly demonstrates that ORCA's ability to stabilize KMT complexes requires its interaction domains. The ~50% reduction is substantial and consistent across methods.

results.result: ORCA depletion causes alterations in DNA replication timing, preferentially affecting late-replicating regions. BrdU immunofluorescence shows dramatic reduction in cells displaying late replication patterns at 8 and 12 hours post-aphidicolin release. Flow cytometry confirms reduced BrdU incorporation without significant changes in early S-phase. Most affected H3K9me3 peaks reside in late-replicating domains, and BrdU ChIP demonstrates changes in replication timing at specific loci (CELSR3, FAM20A) but not at control regions (C-FOS) that lack H3K9 methylation changes.
results.evaluation: Claims C80-C84 establish a link between ORCA-mediated heterochromatin organization and replication timing. The multiple approaches (immunofluorescence, flow cytometry, ChIP-seq correlation, BrdU ChIP) provide converging evidence. The specificity is demonstrated by the unchanged replication timing at C-FOS (C84), suggesting effects are due to heterochromatin disruption rather than direct preRC defects. The correlation between H3K9me3 loss and late-replicating domains (C82) is compelling.

results.result: ORCA's role in heterochromatin organization is independent of its function in preRC assembly. Using a destabilization domain (DD) system to deplete ORCA specifically after G1 phase, the authors show that post-G1 ORCA depletion still causes: (1) reduced H3K9me2 levels, (2) decreased mid- and late-replication patterns with increased early patterns, (3) mislocalization of H3K9me3 and HP1α to perinucleolar rings, and (4) altered BrdU incorporation patterns. Importantly, S-phase progression rates remain comparable between control and ORCA-depleted cells, indicating defects are due to heterochromatin disruption rather than replication defects.
results.evaluation: Claims C85-C92 address a critical question about ORCA's dual roles using an elegant temporal depletion strategy. The DD-ORCA construct is validated by its ability to rescue ORC2 chromatin loading (C85, C86). The observation that depleting ORCA after G1 still causes heterochromatin defects (C87-C90) while S-phase progression is normal (C91) strongly supports the independence of ORCA's heterochromatin function from preRC assembly. This is a key mechanistic insight that separates ORCA's roles in replication licensing versus chromatin organization.

results.result: Background on ORCA: ORCA preferentially localizes to heterochromatic regions in post-replicated cells and associates with centromeric and telomeric heterochromatin. The ORCA-ORC complex binds repressive histone marks (H3K9me3, H3K27me3, H4K20me3). ORCA contains a WD domain crucial for heterochromatin binding and is critical for stabilizing ORC binding to chromatin.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C11-C15 summarize established prior work from the authors and others, appropriately cited. These provide necessary context for the current study but represent background rather than new findings.

results.result: Background on ORC and H3K9 methylation: ORC participates in multiple chromatin functions beyond replication initiation and facilitates HP1 association with H3K9me3-containing heterochromatin. H3K9 methylation exists in mono-, di-, and tri-methyl states with distinct functions, catalyzed by specific KMTs: G9a/GLP for H3K9me2, SETDB1 for H3K9me2/3 in euchromatin, and Suv39H1/H2 for H3K9me3 at heterochromatin.
results.evaluation: Claims C16-C23 provide essential background on ORC functions and H3K9 methylation biology, all appropriately cited to prior literature. This establishes the biological context but represents established knowledge rather than new findings.

results.result: Background on multimeric H3K9 KMT complex: A complex containing all four H3K9 KMTs (G9a, GLP, Suv39H1, SETDB1) has been identified that is recruited to pericentromeric heterochromatin and G9a-repressed gene promoters. Destabilizing any single KMT causes complex disintegration and loss of enzymatic activity. Only ~0.2% of endogenous H3K9 KMTs co-purify with Suv39H1.
results.evaluation: Claims C24-C26, C30 describe prior work on multimeric KMT complexes, appropriately cited to Fritsch et al., 2010. This provides important context for the current findings on ORCA's role in stabilizing these complexes. The quantification (C30) provides a useful comparison point for the current study's findings.

results.result: Recent studies suggest G9a/GLP may participate in pericentric heterochromatin establishment in addition to Suv39H1.
results.evaluation: Claim C37 cites recent literature challenging the traditional view of distinct KMT functions. This provides context for investigating ORCA's interactions with both G9a and Suv39H1 at heterochromatin.

results.result: Discussion and model: The authors propose that ORCA is a scaffold protein that stabilizes the H3K9 KMT complex, and that ORCA recognizes repressive histone marks and recruits KMTs to propagate these marks in a self-sustaining loop mechanism. This is compared to recent work in mouse cells showing ORCA associates with pericentric heterochromatin via H3K9me3.
results.evaluation: Claims C93-C97 represent the authors' interpretation and model based on their experimental findings. The model (C97) is a reasonable synthesis of the data showing ORCA binds methylated histones, recruits/stabilizes KMTs, and that KMT activity is required for ORCA recruitment to heterochromatin. However, C95 is explicitly labeled as speculation, and the self-sustaining loop model (C97), while plausible, involves inference beyond direct demonstration.

results.result: Discussion of H4K20 methylation and other KMTs: H3K9me3 is a prerequisite for H4K20me3 at pericentric heterochromatin. ORCA interacts with Suv420H1/H2 (H4K20 methyltransferases), and Suv420H2 is required for chromatin compaction. H4K20 methylation is crucial for replication origin firing regulation. Other H3K9 mono-methyltransferases (Prdm3, Prdm16, SETDB1) are also implicated in heterochromatin formation.
results.evaluation: Claims C98, C100-C103 cite established literature appropriately. However, C99 states that ORCA interacts with Suv420H1/H2 but notes "data not shown." This is a significant claim relevant to the model but lacks supporting evidence in the manuscript. Without the data, this interaction cannot be evaluated and weakens the discussion of H4K20 methylation's role in the ORCA-mediated pathway.

results.result: Discussion of alternative heterochromatin formation mechanisms: HP1 associates with heterochromatin transiently, pericentric heterochromatin can form independent of Suv39h-HP1, and transcription factor-based mechanisms have been proposed. The authors propose that in human cells, ORCA facilitates heterochromatin recruitment, accumulation, and propagation through a self-sustaining loop mechanism.
results.evaluation: Claims C104-C106 appropriately cite recent literature challenging HP1-centric models of heterochromatin formation, providing context for ORCA as an alternative organizing factor. Claim C107 represents the authors' model, which is a reasonable synthesis of their findings but involves inference and speculation about the complete mechanism.

results.result: Discussion of ORCA's role in ORC recruitment and replication: ORCA facilitates ORC binding to chromatin, and the current data demonstrate ORCA binds H3K9-methylated chromatin and recruits KMTs and ORC/MCM components. The authors speculate that ORCA-mediated epigenetic modifications may provide identity to repressed chromatin crucial for proper replication.
results.evaluation: Claims C108-C109 summarize established and current findings appropriately. Claim C110 is explicitly speculative ("It is possible that...") about the functional significance of linking chromatin modifications to replication, which is reasonable given the data but represents interpretation rather than direct demonstration.

results.result: Discussion of replication timing: G9a mediates H3K9me2 at late-replicating chromatin at the nuclear periphery, and H3K9me2/me3 are enriched at late-replicating facultative/constitutive heterochromatin. The phenotype of ORCA loss is compared to Rif1 loss, which causes similar replication timing changes due to chromatin loop organization defects. The authors propose ORCA functions as a heterochromatin organizer.
results.evaluation: Claims C111-C112 cite established knowledge about H3K9 methylation and replication timing. The comparison to Rif1 (C113) is appropriate and well-cited. The conclusion that ORCA functions as a heterochromatin organizer (C114) is a reasonable inference from the replication timing data combined with the heterochromatin organization defects, though the exact mechanism linking these remains to be fully elucidated.

results.result: Summary conclusions: ORCA is a chromatin reader that facilitates assembly of the writer KMT complex and its partners to specific chromatin sites, regulating DNA replication and heterochromatin organization.
results.evaluation: Claims C115-C116 represent the authors' overall conclusions, which are well-supported by the extensive experimental data presented. The characterization of ORCA as a "reader" (binding methylated histones) that recruits "writers" (KMTs) is accurate and supported. The dual roles in replication and heterochromatin organization are demonstrated, though the mechanistic links between these functions could be further explored.
